title: The four letters, whole
hookLine: Guru Arjan's longing letters to his father, read in full (Majh M5, ang 96–97)

cards: Early in the path we met young Arjan in Lahore. His father, Guru Ram Das, had sent him there for a family wedding and told him to stay until he was called. Weeks went by.
No call came. Arjan wrote home in verse. Tradition says the first two letters never reached his father: his elder brother, Prithi Chand, kept them.
So Arjan numbered the third. When Guru Ram Das read a letter marked three, he asked where one and two had gone. Today, all four stanzas, in order.

teach.h: ONE: I CRY LIKE THE RAINBIRD.
teach.b: They stand in Raag Majh, on angs 96 and 97, as one shabad of four stanzas. The first, in effect: my mind longs for a sight of the Guru.
It cries like the chaatrik, the rainbird that tradition says drinks only falling rain; the thirst won't go, no peace comes, without seeing my beloved.
Each stanza ends: I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the sight of the Guru.

teach.h: TWO: SO LONG SINCE I SAW WATER.
teach.b: The second: your face is beautiful, your words bring a deep, natural peace; it's been so long since this rainbird saw water. The third, the numbered one, is the sharpest.

teach.h: THREE: A MOMENT AWAY IS A DARK AGE.
teach.b: When I can't meet you for even a moment, it's the dark age for me. When will I meet you, beloved? The night won't pass; sleep won't come.
The fourth was written after the reunion. Tradition says Guru Ram Das sent for him, and soon named him the fifth Guru.

teach.h: FOUR: FOUND IN MY OWN HOME.
teach.b: And the last stanza turns: by good fortune I've met the Guru, and found the eternal Lord within my own home.

Read whole, the letters have a shape: longing, then memory, then near despair, then arrival. They can be heard as two loves at once, a son for his father and a soul for the One, and the shabad never pulls the two apart.
Now, the week. The Ardas closed, a whole people's prayer. Then shabad, a hymn for every moment.
Rahao: may I not forget. Lab. Machhuli.
The four watches of a life. And the four letters: longing that gets an answer.

how: Sikhs sing Guru Arjan's Majh shabad 'meraa man lochai gur darsan taaee' in kirtan, and tell the story of the letters from Lahore that led to his being named the fifth Guru.

games.q: you're Arjan in Lahore. two letters have gone unanswered. what do you do?
o: write a third and number it.
games.why: the numbered third letter revealed the missing two. Guru Ram Das called him home.

practice: Bring to mind someone you miss, someone far away, someone you've drifted from, someone who has died, and begin a letter to them in your head the way Arjan did, with the plain truth: I miss you.
Add one thing you remember about them, then what the missing feels like, honestly. If you pray, you can hold them before the One with a quiet Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Darshan, sight, seeing the beloved: Guru Arjan's four stanzas in Raag Majh long for it, like the rainbird, through the third letter's dark night, to the reunion, found in his own home.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sight, seeing the beloved; the letters long for the Guru's darshan.
